court: In the High Court of Madras
advocates: For Respondent: Mr. S. Jayachandran, Government Advocate
judgment_text:
Petition filed under Article 226 of The Constitution of India praying for the issuance of a writ of mandamus directing the respondent to receive and register the settlement deed bearing No. TP/245176180/2026 dated 13.01.2026 in accordance with the provisions of the Registration Act, 1908 within such time as may be stipulated by this Court.

The Order of the Court was delivered by

Senthilkumar Ramamoorthy, J.:— Relying on unregistered Will dated 20.03.2008, the petitioner executed a settlement deed in favour of her son and presented the same for registration. Alleging that no action was taken relating to request for registration, the present writ petition has been filed.

2. Mr. S. Jayachandran, learned Government Advocate, accepts notice for the sole respondent. If the document were to be presented or re-presented, as the case may be, he submits that the document would be registered or a speaking order of refusal would be issued within two weeks.

3. Accordingly, this writ petition is disposed of on the following terms:

3.1 The petitioner shall present or re-present the settlement deed before the registering officer within two weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order;

3.2 Within two weeks therefrom, subject to fulfillment of other requirements relating to registration, the registering officer shall register the document or issue a speaking order of refusal in accordance with Section 71 of the Registration Act, 1908.

There shall be no order as to costs.
